title: CRM Analytics, Tableau, and Data Cloud analytics orientation
objectives: Place core Salesforce reports and dashboards, CRM Analytics, Tableau, and Data Cloud in one orientation map—not as interchangeable names.
Explain CRM Analytics as native CRM analytics that uses datasets, lenses, and often SAQL behind the scenes.
State when Tableau is the complementary enterprise BI choice versus in-CRM analytics.
Treat Data Cloud (also appearing as Data 360 in current Help) as the unified-data foundation, not a report format.
diagnostic_question: A VP hit the 2,000-row report cap, wants multi-cloud customer 360 metrics, and also wants analysts outside Salesforce to explore warehouse data. Do you add another joined report, buy CRM Analytics, bring Tableau, or start with Data Cloud—and what do you refuse to collapse into one buzzword?
definition: Core reports and dashboards query Salesforce objects live with the limits in ANA-005. CRM Analytics (formerly Einstein Analytics / Tableau CRM) is the native analytics experience in Salesforce, with datasets and SAQL behind lenses and dashboards. Tableau is Salesforce's broader BI platform for exploration across many sources. Data Cloud (Help also uses Data 360) unifies customer data that analytics can then consume. ([CRM Analytics Help](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.bi.htm); [SAQL](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.bi_dev_guide_saql.meta/bi_dev_guide_saql/bi_saql_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who call every chart 'Einstein' or who promise a joined report will replace a warehouse. This lesson is orientation: which product family owns the job. It is not a Studio build guide, a Tableau Desktop tutorial, or a Data Cloud implementation plan. Licenses and rebrands change; cite Help and mark SKUs as Needs verification.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of three kitchens on one campus plus a shared walk-in freezer. The diner short-order grill is core reports and dashboards: fast, live CRM tickets, 2,000-row postcards. The in-house tasting lab is CRM Analytics: prepped datasets, lenses, SAQL, insights in the Salesforce flow of work. The city food hall is Tableau: many suppliers, analysts across the company. Data Cloud is the freezer of unified ingredients. You do not grill a banquet for 50,000 guests on the short-order flat-top, and you do not call the freezer a recipe.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce Help's CRM Analytics map is the starting point for datasets, dashboards, recipes, and related Einstein Discovery content. Product names have shifted (Einstein Analytics, Tableau CRM, CRM Analytics); use current Help titles, not a resume of every brand. ([CRM Analytics](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.bi.htm))

The SAQL Developer Guide states that CRM Analytics uses SAQL behind the scenes in lenses, dashboards, and explorer to gather data for visualizations. SAQL queries datasets, not the same metadata as a tabular report. ([SAQL intro](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.bi_dev_guide_saql.meta/bi_dev_guide_saql/bi_saql_intro.htm))

CRM Analytics has its own limitations article; do not assume core report caps (2,000 rows, 5 joined blocks) apply unchanged, and do not assume CRMA removes sharing. ([CRM Analytics Limitations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.bi_limitations.htm))

Tableau is positioned by Salesforce as complementary: CRM Analytics for insights in the CRM workflow; Tableau when you need enterprise BI across functions and sources. Exact packaging (Tableau Cloud versus embedded) is Needs verification per customer contract. Data Cloud / Data 360 is the unification layer Help describes for bringing customer data together for analytics and other uses—not a fourth report format. ([CRM Analytics Help hub](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.bi.htm))

Choose core reports first when the question fits objects, report types, and documented limits. Escalate when you need prepared datasets, multi-source exploration, or a unified profile that reports cannot see. Do not invent connector lists or row-volume SKUs.

mental_model.analogy: Campus kitchens plus a shared walk-in freezer: short-order grill (core reports), tasting lab (CRM Analytics), city food hall (Tableau), freezer (Data Cloud).
useful_mapping: core report → live ticket on the grill
Lightning dashboard → the grill's pass window
CRM Analytics dataset → mise en place in the tasting lab
lens / CRMA dashboard → a tasting plate in Salesforce
SAQL → the lab's recipe language behind the plate
Tableau workbook → a food-hall stall using many suppliers
Data Cloud / Data 360 → unified ingredients in the freezer
2,000-row cap → the grill's ticket printer limit
where_it_breaks: Licenses are not cafeteria meal plans you can assume from the analogy.
Rebrands (Einstein Analytics, Tableau CRM, Data 360) are nameplates, not extra kitchens.
Sharing and FLS still apply; the lab is not a security bypass.
The analogy does not encode SAQL syntax or recipe nodes.

teach_back_prompt: Orient a VP using the campus kitchens: when you stay on the grill, when you use the tasting lab, when you go to the food hall, and what the freezer is. Then name one place the analogy breaks.

Two-minute interview: complementary products, not synonyms.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Core reports are live CRM tickets with tight caps. CRM Analytics is native dataset analytics with SAQL in Salesforce. Tableau is broader enterprise BI. Data Cloud unifies data those tools can use. They are complementary, not four names for one report.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the job. If a report type, filter, and Lightning dashboard answer it inside ANA-005 limits, I stay there. If they need prepared datasets and in-app exploration, I orient to CRM Analytics and mention SAQL and the CRMA limitations article. If analysts live outside Salesforce on many sources, I orient to Tableau. If the real gap is a unified profile no object graph has, I orient to Data Cloud first. I refuse to 'just add a joined report' as a warehouse. I mark licenses as Needs verification.

terminology.plain: Salesforce's native analytics product for CRM-context datasets, lenses, and dashboards.
terminology.precise: Documented in Help as its own map (sf.bi.htm). Formerly Einstein Analytics and Tableau CRM in earlier branding.
terminology.example: A sales app with a dataset of Opportunities plus related objects explored in a CRMA dashboard.
terminology.boundary: This lesson orients; it does not teach recipe nodes.

terminology.plain: A prepared collection of data CRMA queries, not a live report type.
terminology.precise: SAQL runs against datasets. Building datasets is a CRMA job, not New Report.
terminology.example: A nightly dataset combining Account and Opportunity fields for exploration.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Reporting snapshot (a core-reports feature with its own allocation in ANA-005's limits table).
terminology.boundary: Freshness depends on sync/recipe design—Needs verification per org.

terminology.plain: The query language CRM Analytics uses against datasets.
terminology.precise: Developer Guide: used behind lenses, dashboards, and explorer.
terminology.example: A lens that filters a dataset with SAQL generated by the explorer.
terminology.non_example: A row-level formula on a Lightning report (ANA-003).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SOQL: Apex/API query language for sObjects, not CRMA datasets.
terminology.boundary: Do not write SAQL in this lesson; know where it lives.

terminology.plain: Salesforce's broader visual analytics / BI platform for many sources and audiences.
terminology.precise: Complementary to CRM Analytics: use Tableau when insight is needed across the enterprise, not only in CRM workflow. Exact edition is contractual.
terminology.example: Finance exploring warehouse plus Salesforce extracts in Tableau Cloud.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Tableau CRM (old name for CRM Analytics)—do not mix the names in an interview.
terminology.boundary: Tableau Desktop how-to is out of scope.

terminology.plain: The unification layer for customer data that analytics and other products can use.
terminology.precise: Help and product docs also say Data 360. It is not a tabular/summary/matrix/joined format.
terminology.example: Harmonized profiles from CRM plus web plus service that a CRMA dataset or Tableau source can read.
terminology.non_example: A custom report type with two objects.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Data Loader (DATA track): bulk CRUD, not a CDP.
terminology.boundary: Implementation, identity resolution, and SKUs: Needs verification.

terminology.plain: A CRMA exploration saved from explorer, backed by SAQL on a dataset.
terminology.precise: Developer Guide lists lenses among the places SAQL runs.
terminology.example: An Opportunity-amount-by-segment lens in Analytics Studio.
terminology.boundary: UI names in Studio can change; confirm in-org.

terminology.plain: The report builder and Lightning dashboards taught in ANA-001–005.
terminology.precise: Live (or cached per platform) queries of Salesforce objects through report types, with the limits Help lists.
terminology.example: A summary Opportunities report on a specified-user dashboard.
terminology.non_example: A CRMA dashboard on a dataset.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Reporting snapshots, which copy report results to a custom object on a schedule (limits table)—not CRMA.
terminology.boundary: Stay here until a documented cap or data-scope gap forces orientation.

terminology.plain: A related predictive feature in the CRM Analytics family Help map.
terminology.precise: Help links Einstein Discovery from the CRMA hub. It is not a report format and not Tableau Desktop.
terminology.example: A model that predicts win likelihood, later embedded—implementation is out of scope.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Einstein Report Formula Generation on core reports (neighboring generative feature).
terminology.boundary: Do not claim every org has Discovery.

when_to_use: When core reports hit documented limits or cannot see multi-cloud unified profiles, and you must orient to CRM Analytics, Tableau, or Data Cloud.
When an interviewer asks how CRM Analytics differs from Lightning reports, including SAQL on datasets.
When someone uses the old names Einstein Analytics or Tableau CRM and you must map them to CRM Analytics.
When Data Cloud / Data 360 is proposed as 'just another report type' and you must refuse that collapse.
when_not_to_use: Do not use CRM Analytics as the answer to a missing field on a custom report type (ANA-001).
Do not use Tableau as a synonym for a Lightning dashboard widget (ANA-004).
Do not use Data Cloud as a workaround for sharing or the 2,000-row cap without an architecture review.
Do not teach SAQL syntax, Tableau calculations, or Data Cloud identity resolution in this orientation lesson.

License and SKU facts are Needs verification.

interview_questions.question: How do core reports, CRM Analytics, Tableau, and Data Cloud differ?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Core reports query Salesforce objects live with tight caps. CRM Analytics is native dataset analytics with SAQL. Tableau is complementary enterprise BI. Data Cloud unifies data. They are not four names for one chart.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from the job. Operational CRM lists stay on report types and Lightning dashboards. Prepared in-Salesforce exploration is CRM Analytics—Help hub plus a separate limitations article. Multi-source analysts point to Tableau, and I will not call it Tableau CRM. If the profile does not exist on objects, Data Cloud / Data 360 comes first. Licenses are Needs verification. I never promise a joined report as a warehouse.
interview_questions.example: This-quarter pipeline on core reports; two-year mixed sources oriented to CRMA/Tableau; web+CRM profile oriented to Data Cloud.
tradeoffs: Time-to-value on core reports vs licensed platforms

interview_questions.question: What is SAQL and where does it run?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: SAQL is the CRM Analytics query language for datasets. The Developer Guide says it runs behind lenses, dashboards, and explorer. It is not SOQL and not a Lightning row-level formula.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I only need the mental model in this interview: datasets in, visualizations out, SAQL in the middle. I do not write a SAQL script on a whiteboard unless they ask a CRMA-developer follow-up. I contrast SOQL for sObjects. I mention the CRMA limitations article so they know caps differ from 2,000-row reports. I refuse to paste SAQL into a validation rule.
interview_questions.example: A lens in Analytics Studio exploring an Opportunity dataset, SAQL generated by explorer.

interview_questions.question: A VP wants one joined report of CRM, marketing cloud events, and a warehouse. Answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A joined report only combines Salesforce report types, max five blocks, with core caps. I orient to Data Cloud for unification and Tableau or CRMA for exploration, with licenses Needs verification.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw the campus kitchens. The grill cannot take three clouds. If events are not objects with relationships, ANA-001 cannot save us. I split: operational CRM stays on reports; unified profile is Data Cloud; analysts may use Tableau; in-app CRM exploration may be CRMA. I document that I am not implementing identity resolution in this meeting. I will not sell a sixth joined block.
interview_questions.example: Orientation memo with four headings and two Help URLs.
follow_ups: What if they already own Tableau Cloud?
Reporting snapshots as a halfway house?

interview_questions.question: They say they 'already have Tableau' but they mean Lightning dashboards. How do you untangle it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I ask which UI they open: Reports tab, Analytics Studio, or Tableau Cloud. Tableau CRM was the old CRMA name. Lightning dashboards are core reports (ANA-004).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Name confusion is the whole job. I walk them to the product. If they are on Dashboards with widgets and a running user, that is ANA-004. If they are in Studio on datasets, that is CRMA. If they have Tableau workbooks on many sources, that is Tableau. I write the former names on the board so the next meeting uses one vocabulary. I still do not quote SKUs.

tradeoffs: Retraining names vs buying another tool
follow_ups: How to tell a CRMA dashboard from a Lightning one?

interview_questions.question: Analytics Studio is missing. Is CRM Analytics retired?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Usually it is a license or permission gap, not a retired product. The Help hub still documents CRM Analytics. I check assignments and do not promise a SKU.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open sf.bi.htm with them. I check permission sets and whether the org ever bought CRMA. I look at App Launcher for Analytics. If unlicensed, the orientation still matters for roadmap. I do not 'enable Einstein' in production from a hallway request. I also check they are not looking for Tableau Cloud in a Salesforce org search box.
interview_questions.example: Sandbox without CRMA licenses; Help hub still used for the four-family map.
tradeoffs: Stay on core reports vs purchase
Permission fix vs true unlicensed org
follow_ups: Which permission set names? Needs verification.

interview_questions.question: A developer writes SAQL in a Lightning row-level formula. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Wrong language and wrong product. Row-level formulas use the report formula functions. SAQL queries CRMA datasets in lenses and CRMA dashboards.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show ANA-003 versus the SAQL guide. PARENTGROUPVAL is a summary formula function on grouped reports. SAQL is not valid there. If they need dataset math, they are in Studio. If they need per-Opportunity days to close, they stay on a row-level formula or an object field. Mixing languages is a common interview fail I can catch in code review too.
interview_questions.example: Rejecting a pull request that pasted SAQL into a report formula editor.
tradeoffs: Object formula vs row-level vs dataset

interview_questions.question: How do you decide the sequence: reports, CRMA, Tableau, Data Cloud?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Prove core reports first. If you need in-CRM datasets, CRMA. If you need enterprise multi-source BI, Tableau. If you need a unified profile, Data Cloud before pretty charts. Licenses last, not first, but they can block.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Sequence prevents shopping. I write the gap: cap, missing object, extra audience, or extra source. Caps and missing objects sometimes still stay in core (filters, CRT). Extra audience plus extra source leans Tableau. Extra source that must become a profile leans Data Cloud. In-CRM exploration leans CRMA. I put security beside every step so nobody uses a dataset to launder View All Data. I mark SKUs Needs verification after the design, not as the design.
interview_questions.example: Pipeline stays; CMO profile waits on Data Cloud; Strategy waits on Tableau contract.
tradeoffs: One vendor story vs honest gaps

interview_questions.question: Teach the four families with the campus kitchens and break the analogy.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Grill is core reports, tasting lab is CRM Analytics with SAQL, food hall is Tableau, freezer is Data Cloud. The analogy breaks on licenses, rebrands, and sharing—none of those are meal plans.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add that Tableau CRM is a lab nameplate, not the food hall. I cite the SAQL guide and CRMA limitations article. I refuse a library story. I finish: if the ticket is a missing CRT field, go back to the grill, do not open a new restaurant.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard four stations plus a 'Needs verification' sticky on the cash register.
follow_ups: Where does the kitchen analogy break?
